thedford: Thedford, Nebraska, a tiny Sandhills town on the Middle Loup River: a few clapboard houses and a white wooden grain elevator among grass-covered dunes, a line of cottonwoods along the river.
dismal: The Dismal River in the Nebraska Sandhills: a clear, fast, narrow river cutting a sandy little canyon through grass-covered dunes, an old rusted steel truss bridge standing over it with no road leading to it.
broken-bow: Broken Bow, Nebraska: the town square, a red-brick and stone county courthouse in a park of old elm trees, brick storefronts around the square kept clean and unused, deep grass in the street.
loup-fog: The North Loup River valley at dawn in thick fog: braided channels and pale sandbars, cottonwoods ghostly in the mist, a center-pivot irrigation arm standing still in a field beyond.
archway: The Great Platte River Road Archway near Kearney, Nebraska: the big brown timber-and-steel monument building that spans the interstate, the highway beneath it gone to tall grass and wildflowers, no cars.
columbus: The meeting of the Loup and Platte rivers near Columbus, Nebraska: wide sandy channels joining, cottonwoods, the tall stacks of a long-quiet power plant on the horizon.
omaha: Downtown Omaha, Nebraska seen across the Missouri River: the office towers kept but quiet, trees growing on terraces and rooftops, the wide brown river, a flagpole flying a plain gray flag with a single white circle in the middle.
bridge: The Bob Kerrey pedestrian bridge, a white S-curving cable-stayed footbridge over the Missouri River between Omaha and Council Bluffs, empty, early morning, mist on the water.
scottsbluff: Scotts Bluff in western Nebraska: the great tan sandstone bluff rising above the North Platte valley, old wagon-trail ruts worn into the grass in the foreground.
niobrara: The Niobrara River near Valentine, Nebraska: a shallow sandy river in a canyon with pine-covered cliffs, a thin waterfall falling down a mossy side canyon.
kingsley: Kingsley Dam and Lake McConaughy, Nebraska: the long grassy earthen dam and its tall concrete intake tower, the huge blue lake and its white sand beaches, empty.
